records.name: Bhuvanagiri Hill
records.description: A prominent monolithic hill crowned by Bhuvanagiri Fort. Telangana Tourism gives the hill's height as 610 metres; this record documents the named hill and the published elevation, not a claim that it is the state's highest point.
records.referenceDate: Official Telangana Tourism destination profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Forest ecosystems of Uttar Pradesh
records.description: The Forest Survey of India’s 2019 State of Forest Report classifies Uttar Pradesh’s forests into five Champion and Seth forest-type groups and 28 forest types. Reported types include Northern Dry Mixed Deciduous Forest, Anogeissus pendula Forest, Dry Siwalik Sal Forest, Western and Eastern Alluvial Plains Sal Forests, swamp forest and alluvial grassland. This is a forest-ecosystem profile, not a complete inventory of all state ecosystems.
records.referenceDate: ISFR 2019, Volume II, Chapter 11.28, especially section 11.28.3 and Table 11.28.9

records.regionName: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
records.name: Forest ecosystems — Dadra and Nagar Haveli component
records.description: The Forest Survey of India’s 2019 State of Forest Report identifies two forest-type groups in the former Dadra and Nagar Haveli Union Territory: Tropical Moist Deciduous Forests and Tropical Dry Deciduous Forests, represented by four forest types. The cited chapter covers Dadra and Nagar Haveli only, not the former Daman and Diu districts; this entry is scoped to that component of the present merged Union Territory.
records.referenceDate: ISFR 2019, Volume II, Chapter 11.33, sections 11.33.1 and 11.33.3

records.name: Forest ecosystems of Bihar
records.description: The Forest Survey of India (FSI) classifies Bihar's forests into four Champion and Seth forest-type groups and 13 forest types. Sal forests occur in the Terai of West Champaran (moist deciduous) and in southern districts including Kaimur, Rohtas, Gaya, Jamui, Munger and Banka (dry deciduous).
records.referenceDate: ISFR 2019, Volume II, Chapter 11.4; accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Forest ecosystems of Goa
records.description: FSI identifies five forest-type groups and five forest types in Goa. The report describes plateau vegetation across undulating terrain and hills and records 16 mangrove species, including Rhizophora, Bruguiera, Avicennia and Sonneratia.
records.referenceDate: ISFR 2019, Volume II, Chapter 11.7; accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Forest ecosystems of Haryana
records.description: FSI identifies three forest-type groups in Haryana: Tropical Dry Deciduous, Tropical Thorn and Subtropical Pine, divided into ten forest types. The report also notes the State's extensive agroforestry landscape.
records.referenceDate: ISFR 2019, Volume II, Chapter 11.9; accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Forest ecosystems of Jharkhand
records.description: FSI identifies two forest-type groups in Jharkhand, divided into eight forest types. The report describes a forest-rich plateau landscape, with tropical moist deciduous and tropical dry deciduous formations.
records.referenceDate: ISFR 2019, Volume II, Chapter 11.12; accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Forest ecosystems of Maharashtra
records.description: FSI identifies six forest-type groups in Maharashtra, divided into 17 forest types. The mapped formations include West Coast Semi-Evergreen, Southern Moist Mixed Deciduous, mangrove, littoral, riparian, dry teak, dry bamboo and Western Subtropical Hill Forest.
records.referenceDate: ISFR 2019, Volume II, Chapter 11.16; accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Forest ecosystems of Manipur
records.description: FSI's forest-type mapping for Manipur includes Cachar Semi-Evergreen Forest, Secondary Moist Bamboo Brakes, East Himalayan Moist Mixed Deciduous Forest, Eastern Wet Alluvial Grassland, East Himalayan and Khasi Sub-Tropical Wet Hill Forests, Naga Hill Wet Temperate Forest and Montane Bamboo Brakes.
records.referenceDate: ISFR 2019, Volume II, Chapter 11.17; accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Forest ecosystems of Mizoram
records.description: FSI's Champion and Seth forest-type mapping and biodiversity assessment for Mizoram records tropical semi-evergreen, tropical moist deciduous and subtropical pine forest groups. The rapid assessment observed 87 tree, 96 shrub and 56 herb species; these are survey observations, not a complete species inventory.
records.referenceDate: ISFR 2019, Volume II, Chapter 11.19; accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Forest ecosystems of Nagaland
records.description: FSI's forest-type mapping for Nagaland classifies forest formations under the Champion and Seth system. Its rapid biodiversity assessment observed 56 tree, 137 shrub and 113 herb species; these are survey observations, not a complete species inventory.
records.referenceDate: ISFR 2019, Volume II, Chapter 11.20; accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Forest ecosystems of Punjab
records.description: FSI's forest-type mapping for Punjab records Northern Dry Mixed Deciduous Forest, Dry Deciduous Scrub, Dry Bamboo Brakes, Anogeissus pendula Forest and Scrub, Ravine Thorn Forest, Desert Thorn Forest and Siwalik Chir Pine Forest, alongside plantation/tree cover outside forests.
records.referenceDate: ISFR 2019, Volume II, Chapter 11.22; accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Forest ecosystems of Rajasthan
records.description: FSI's mapped forest types in Rajasthan include Northern Dry Mixed Deciduous Forest, Anogeissus pendula Forest and Scrub, Very Dry and Dry Teak Forest, Dry Savannah Forest, Boswellia Forest, Butea Forest, Aegle Forest, Phoenix Savannah Forest and Dry Tropical Riverain Forest.
records.referenceDate: ISFR 2019, Volume II, Chapter 11.23; accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Forest ecosystems of Telangana
records.description: FSI's 2019 forest-cover type table for Telangana reports Southern Dry Mixed Deciduous Forest (60.52%), Dry Deciduous Scrub (19.21%), Dry Teak Forest (14.84%) and smaller mapped areas of Southern Moist Mixed Deciduous Forest, bamboo brakes and other types. Percentages refer to the report's mapped forest-cover classes.
records.referenceDate: ISFR 2019, Volume II, Chapter 11.26; accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Forest ecosystems of Tripura
records.description: FSI's mapped forest types in Tripura include Cachar Semi-Evergreen Forest, Secondary Moist Bamboo Brakes, East Himalayan Lower Bhabar Sal and East Himalayan Moist Mixed Deciduous Forest, with plantation/tree cover outside forests separately reported.
records.referenceDate: ISFR 2019, Volume II, Chapter 11.27; accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Forest ecosystems of Delhi
records.description: FSI identifies Tropical Dry Deciduous and Tropical Thorn forest groups in Delhi. Its rapid biodiversity assessment observed 16 tree, 11 shrub and 36 herb species; the figures describe the report's survey, not a complete species inventory.
records.referenceDate: ISFR 2019, Volume II, Chapter 11.6; accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Forest ecosystems of Jammu and Kashmir
records.description: The FSI chapter covers the former combined Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh area and does not disaggregate its forest-type percentages by today's Union Territory boundaries. The combined mapping includes Northern Dry Mixed Deciduous, Siwalik and Himalayan Chir Pine, Himalayan Subtropical Scrub, Olea cuspidata Scrub, Dwarf Rhododendron Scrub, Alpine Pastures and Dry Alpine Scrub.
records.referenceDate: ISFR 2019, Volume II, Chapter 11.11; accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Forest ecosystems of Ladakh
records.description: The FSI chapter covers the former combined Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh area and does not disaggregate its forest-type percentages by today's Union Territory boundaries. The combined mapping includes Himalayan Dry Temperate and Alpine formations, including Alpine Pastures, Dry Alpine Scrub and Dwarf Juniper Scrub; this entry must not be read as a Ladakh-only percentage profile.
records.referenceDate: ISFR 2019, Volume II, Chapter 11.11; accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Forest ecosystems of Chandigarh
records.description: FSI's forest-type classification for Chandigarh includes Group 5 Tropical Dry Deciduous Forests. Its rapid biodiversity assessment observed 21 tree, 4 shrub and 7 herb species; these are survey observations, not a complete species inventory.
records.referenceDate: ISFR 2019, Volume II, Chapter 11.32; accessed 31 October 2026

records.regionName: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
records.name: Forest ecosystems of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
records.description: The FSI chapter for the former Daman and Diu Union Territory identifies Littoral Forest, Mangrove Forest, Southern Dry Mixed Deciduous Forest, Dry Deciduous Scrub and Desert Thorn Forest, with plantation/tree cover outside forests reported separately. This entry covers the Daman and Diu component only; Dadra and Nagar Haveli is documented in a separate record.
records.referenceDate: ISFR 2019, Volume II, Chapter 11.34; accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Forest ecosystems of Lakshadweep
records.description: FSI's forest-type table for Lakshadweep reports Plantation/Tree Outside Forest (TOF) as 100% of the mapped forest-cover type. This is a specific classification result and should not be interpreted as evidence of natural forest formations.
records.referenceDate: ISFR 2019, Volume II, Chapter 11.35; accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Forest ecosystems of Puducherry
records.description: FSI's forest-type table for Puducherry reports Mangrove Forest at 3.19% and Plantation/Tree Outside Forest (TOF) at 96.81% of mapped forest cover. The figures are from the 2019 report's forest-type mapping.
records.referenceDate: ISFR 2019, Volume II, Chapter 11.36; accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Subansiri Lower Hydroelectric Project
records.description: A 1,250 MW run-of-river hydropower project on the Subansiri River, located on the Arunachal Pradesh–Assam border. NHPC lists the project under Arunachal Pradesh and Assam; this entry records its Arunachal Pradesh location and cross-border setting.
records.referenceDate: NHPC project portfolio, accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Minimata Hasdeo Bango Project
records.description: The Minimata Hasdeo Bango Dam and reservoir on the Hasdeo system is a major state water-resources project. The Chhattisgarh Government reports a live storage capacity of 2,894.33 million cubic metres and gross storage of 3,264.33 million cubic metres; the figures are reservoir capacities, not annual flows.
records.referenceDate: Chhattisgarh Government project information, accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Salaulim Dam Irrigation Project
records.description: The Salaulim Dam on the Salaulim River, a tributary of the Zuari, is an integral component of Goa's irrigation project and is also used for drinking-water supply.
records.referenceDate: Government of Goa dam profile, accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Chamera-I Hydroelectric Project
records.description: NHPC's Chamera-I Power Station is located in Chamba district on the Ravi River. The three-unit station has an installed capacity of 540 MW and was commissioned in 1994.
records.referenceDate: NHPC Chamera-I project profile, accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Loktak Hydroelectric Project
records.description: NHPC lists the Loktak Power Station in Manipur with three 35 MW units (105 MW total); the station was commissioned in 1983.
records.referenceDate: NHPC official project and power-station portfolio, accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Umiam–Umtru Hydroelectric Scheme
records.description: Meghalaya's 2024 Power Policy lists the Umiam Stage I–IV stations at 36, 20, 60 and 60 MW respectively, alongside other hydro stations in the state. The four Umiam stages therefore total 176 MW of installed capacity.
records.referenceDate: Meghalaya Power Policy 2024, existing power plants table

records.name: Tuirial Hydroelectric Project
records.description: NEEPCO lists the Tuirial Hydro Power Station in Kolasib district, Mizoram, with two 30 MW units (60 MW total); it entered commercial operation in 2018.
records.referenceDate: NEEPCO Hydro Power Stations portfolio, updated 24 April 2026

records.name: Doyang Hydroelectric Project
records.description: NEEPCO lists the Doyang Hydro Power Station in Wokha district, Nagaland, with three 25 MW units (75 MW total).
records.referenceDate: NEEPCO Hydro Power Stations portfolio, updated 24 April 2026

records.name: Bhakra–Beas Multipurpose River Valley System
records.description: The BBMB project history describes the integrated Bhakra–Nangal, Beas and Ravi development system for irrigation and power generation, including the Bhakra Dam on the Sutlej and the Beas–Sutlej link. The system is interstate; its benefits and canal network extend into Punjab and neighboring states, while individual dams are not all located within Punjab.
records.referenceDate: BBMB official project history, accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Teesta-V Hydroelectric Project
records.description: NHPC lists Teesta-V in Sikkim as a commissioned 510 MW power station (three 170 MW units), commissioned in 2008.
records.referenceDate: NHPC official project and power-station portfolio, accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Gumti Hydroelectric Project
records.description: The Central Electricity Authority's Tripura hydro profile states that no large hydroelectric project has been identified in the State, but records the Gumti Hydroelectric Project in South Tripura as a 15 MW station (three 5 MW units) on the Gumti River, installed in 1976 and 1984.
records.referenceDate: CEA State Profile on Hydro Development for Tripura, 18 November 2024

records.name: Kalpong Hydroelectric Project
records.description: NHPC describes the 5.25 MW Kalpong Hydroelectric Project as the first hydropower project executed and commissioned for the Andaman and Nicobar Administration, providing a local renewable electricity source.
records.referenceDate: NHPC Kalpong project profile, accessed 31 October 2026

records.regionName: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
records.name: Damanganga Reservoir Project (Madhuban Dam)
records.description: The Damanganga Reservoir Project agreement was made among Gujarat, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Daman and Diu. The dam is at Madhuban in Valsad district, Gujarat; the project agreement identifies both Union Territories as beneficiaries and provides for irrigation, domestic/industrial water supply and incidental hydropower. This is an inter-governmental beneficiary project, not a dam located inside the UT.
records.referenceDate: Inter-governmental agreement dated 29 September 1992

records.name: Salal Hydroelectric Project
records.description: NHPC lists the Salal Power Station on the Chenab in the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir, with six 115 MW units (690 MW total), commissioned in 1987.
records.referenceDate: NHPC official project and power-station portfolio, accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Nimoo-Bazgo Hydroelectric Project
records.description: NHPC's Nimoo-Bazgo station is a 45 MW run-of-river scheme on the Indus near Alchi in Leh district, Ladakh. The three 15 MW units were commissioned in 2012–13.
records.referenceDate: NHPC official project and power-station portfolio, accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: 2019 Composite Disaster Risk Index
records.description: The 2019 MHA/UNDP-supported sub-national study reports a Composite Disaster Risk Index of 27.58 on a 0–100 scale for Andhra Pradesh. This is a historical, methodology-specific composite index combining hazard, vulnerability, exposure and capacity; it is not a current forecast or a district-level hazard classification.
records.referenceDate: MHA/UNDP-supported sub-national disaster risk study, 2019, Table 1.6

records.name: 2019 Composite Disaster Risk Index — historical UT components
records.description: The 2019 study predates the merger of Dadra and Nagar Haveli with Daman and Diu. It reports separate Composite Disaster Risk Index values: 9.91 for Dadra and Nagar Haveli and 10.20 for Daman and Diu, each on a 0–100 scale. No combined score is published; the two historical component values are retained separately without averaging. These are historical composite indices, not current hazard forecasts.
records.referenceDate: MHA/UNDP-supported sub-national disaster risk study, 2019, Table 1.6

records.name: Separate 2019 Disaster Risk Index not reported for Ladakh
records.description: The 2019 study does not publish a separate Ladakh score. Ladakh was included within the then combined Jammu and Kashmir state entry (Composite Disaster Risk Index 14.56); that former-state value must not be presented as a Ladakh-only score.
records.referenceDate: MHA/UNDP-supported sub-national disaster risk study, 2019, Table 1.6
